Bridges, tunnels and rivers: what is wrong and how to build them once

data: today's main (22969ae), streets and walks rebuilt for La Habana, Matanzas and Mayabeque

Most of what the player meets on a bridge or in a tunnel comes from five causes in the code, not from the single structures: twin tubes built at two depths, ramps that spill onto the ground streets, bridges that know about streets but not about rivers or valleys, a province clip that drops border bridges, and no inland water at all. This page shows each one with shots and wheel profiles, then proposes one design that removes all five.

01What was found

  • The 5ta Avenida tunnel is one box holding two bores at −14 m and −7.7 m. Inside, the roof slabs of the two bores sit at different heights, with wedges of sky between them and a slanted slab across the road: the "pieces of street in the middle". Its approach is a trench 16 m deep and about 200 m long on the Miramar side.
  • The Línea tunnel drives without steps, but has the same roof gaps between its bores.
  • The Bay tunnel is tagged layer −3 for one bore and −1 for the other and its access ramps. The game builds each layer apart, so the ramps meet the tube with steps of up to 8.1 m.
  • The Almendares bridges (Hierro, Calle 23, Calle 11, 7ma) stand on dry ground: the river is not drawn and the relief under them is 1-6 m. Puente de Hierro's deck is under 1.5 m over the grass. Calle 23's deck has 1.5 m humps where it clears the streets below it.
  • Bacunayagua (313 m, 103.5 m high in OSM) does not exist in the game, and neither does its gorge: the 90 m relief smooths it into hills.
  • In Matanzas, Calixto García has a 5.3 m drop where its ramp ends, and the San Juan and Yumurí are not drawn: their beds lie 1-3 m over sea level, above the 0.3 m threshold that makes water.
  • Canímar and the Guanima and Matanzas-Varadero viaducts drive cleanly (no step over 15 cm), but stand over dry, shallow valleys.

02Method

For each structure: the OSM ways and tags read from cuba-latest.osm.pbf with pyosmium; the game's road graph (g_way keeps the OSM id) to find the edges, extended 150-300 m along the straightest street at each end; a wheel driven along the right-hand lane every 0.5 m on Surface.height(x, z, near=previous), as the car does; and offscreen shots with a free camera (approach, on the deck or inside, two sides from 30 m up, the portals from above). A step is a change over 15 cm in 0.5 m (a ramp at 8 % changes 4 cm). A seam is a 1-8 cm wobble off the smoothed profile.

The provinces' streets, structures and walks were rebuilt with today's code before probing (the Nov 19 tunnel fixes are in). The shots use the same data. What was not checked: the car's physics on the steps (only the surface), and night lighting in tunnels.

OSM tags only the covered part as a tunnel and only the span as a bridge. The approach ramps are ordinary ways at layer 0. OSM's layer orders crossings at one spot. It is not a depth: the Bay tunnel's −3 and −1 say nothing about one bore being deeper. Some ways carry real measurements (height, length, width) that the game does not read.

04The Almendares tunnels

Causes, in contravia/streets.py and contravia/structures.py:

  • structure_profile sets a tunnel's depth per carriageway: raw − TUNNEL_DEPTH (8 m under the ground) where the relief is over SEA (0.3 m), and −SEA_DEPTH (−14 m) where it is under. At the Almendares mouth one bore's centreline crosses relief under 0.3 m and the other's, a few metres away, does not: a 6.3 m jump in the rule turns into a 6.3 m difference between the bores.
  • _twin then joins the bores into one box (closer than TWIN = 12 m), with no wall between them. Each bore keeps its own roof at its own floor + 5.5 m, and _between draws the step between the two floors and the two roofs. That step is the slab across the road, and the gap between roofs is where the sky shows.
  • A tunnel's ends sit at full depth at OSM's portal (np.minimum(lin, need + GRADE·d) with need = −8 m at the ends). The ground streets that leave from it ramp down at 8 % (_ramp_to), and a ramp too long for its street is carried through the next junction (CARRY), easing the side streets of that junction down with it. That makes the long trenches and the cross streets that dip into the ground.

05The Almendares bridges

Cause: a bridge's profile is the highest of the straight line between its ends, the ground, and 6 m (BRIDGE_CLEAR) over every street or junction under it, climbing at 8 %. Water is not among the things it clears, so over the river it follows the ground (dry in the game). Each street below makes its own peak, hence the humps. The relief here is 30 m per sample, too coarse for a river 40 m wide.

06The Bay tunnel

Cause: streets.build builds each OSM layer as a separate level, and heights settles them one at a time (for L in sorted(...)). The −1 links and the −1 bore are settled before the −3 bore exists, so their ends cannot agree with it. A junction on a level takes the mean height of its streets' ends, which averages a deep bore and a shallow link into a step. The surface then picks among stacked triangles by near + STEP (1.5 m), so at a step larger than that the wheel lands on whichever level is nearest its last height: the 1-8 m jumps around the harbour.

07Matanzas and Bacunayagua

Bacunayagua is missing for a reason that has nothing to do with bridges. graph.build_graph keeps a way in a province when its midpoint is inside the province (Matanzas, for this bridge), then keeps only the largest strongly connected part. The bridge's west end continues into Mayabeque, which is not in Matanzas' graph, so in Matanzas the bridge and its approaches lead nowhere and are dropped. In Mayabeque they are outside the province. Every road that crosses a province border loses the pieces up to its first junction on each side; here that is 1.1 km. The gorge is missing because the relief there has a 90 m step and the gorge, about 300 m wide at the road and 100 m deep, spans three or four samples.

08Rivers and water

The game draws water in one way: a plane at WATER_Y (0.1 m) where the relief is under SEA (0.3 m), shaped by the coast and the shore. OSM's rivers and lakes are read only to keep buildings off them (NOT_BUILT in prepare.py), and WorldCover's water class is left out of the ground colours. The relief along every river checked:

10Proposed design

One idea runs through it: a bridge or a tunnel is an object built from what it crosses, with its own approaches, not a street whose height is patched after the fact. The streets module then stops guessing levels; it asks the structure.

1. Structures as objects, found before the graph is cut into levels

Group OSM ways into structures: ways with the same bridge/tunnel tag joined end to end, plus the parallel carriageway within 30 m with the same name (the two bores of a tunnel, the two decks of a bridge). Add the approach: the ways on each side up to the point where the structure's height meets the ground at the allowed grade, following the straightest street (as the probe does). A structure holds its carriageways, its approaches, its cross-section type and one profile shared by all its carriageways. OSM's layer is used only to order structures that cross each other, never as a level of its own.

2. One profile per structure, solved from what it crosses

Each structure gets a single vertical profile along its axis, the smoothest line (least curvature, grade at most 6 % for motorways and 8 % elsewhere) that satisfies, at every sample:

  • a bridge: deck ≥ crossed street + 6 m, ≥ water surface + clearance (2 m for a stream, 5 m for a river, OSM's height when tagged: 103.5 m at Bacunayagua), ≥ ground + 1 m; a road under a bridge is never raised to meet it;
  • a tunnel: roof ≤ ground − 1.5 m of cover, ≤ river bed or sea floor − 2 m (the floor then follows from the roof minus 5.5 m), with one continuous rule instead of the jump at 0.3 m;
  • both: equal to the ground street's own height at the far end of each approach.

With vertical curves at each change of grade (a parabola over 30-60 m) the profile has no humps or kinks. It is a small 1-D problem per structure (a few hundred samples): a bounded least-squares solve, or the current max/min envelope followed by a curvature smoothing pass that keeps the bounds. Both carriageways read the same profile, so twin bores and twin decks can never differ in height.

3. Approaches belong to the structure

The ramp is part of the structure: an open cut with retaining walls for a tunnel, an embankment or a ramp on walls for a bridge, drawn by structures.py. A street that meets the approach does one of two things, decided once: it crosses over it (OSM says so: Calle 11 and 7ma over the 5ta approach, the Malecón end) and becomes a small bridge at ground height, or it ends at the approach's wall in a T. No easing of side streets, no ramp carried through junctions. A junction on a structure takes the structure's height at that point, never a mean.

4. The wheel stays on the structure it is on

Every street and structure triangle carries a structure id (0 for ground). The wheel keeps the id it stands on and, where triangles overlap, prefers the same id, then any piece connected to it at its edge (the approach, the ground street at the end). The 1.5 m near rule stays only as a fallback. This removes the harbour jumps even where geometry is imperfect, and makes the probe of section 02 a test: no step over 5 cm along any structure on the island.

5. Water as a layer of its own

  • Read natural=water areas (ways and multipolygon relations, water=river|lake|reservoir|pond) and waterway=river|stream|canal lines buffered by OSM's width, or by class (river 20 m, canal 8 m, stream 4 m). Store them in a water.src beside coast.src, as the shore and causeways do.
  • Carve them into the relief: lower the ground inside the channel to a bed 1.5-3 m under the banks, with banks sloping over 5-10 m. This also brings back the gorges the 90 m relief smooths (Bacunayagua, Canímar, Yumurí), with OSM's bridge height as a check of the gorge depth.
  • Draw a water surface per river, flat across and stepping down along the river in short reaches, with the sea's water material. Lakes and reservoirs get one flat level each.
  • The car treats it like the sea (sea.py): it sinks and comes back on the nearest road.

6. Dressing from the tags

  • Bridges: piers placed at the banks and at even spans between them (never in the channel when the span allows), abutments at the ends, a parapet or a metal railing by class and surface, lamps where lit=yes. A few named templates: a concrete arch for Bacunayagua, steel trusses for Concordia and Calixto García, the swing span for Puente de Hierro.
  • Tunnels: one box per structure with a single roof over all bores, a central wall with openings where bores are separate, a portal face with the name, tiled walls up to 2 m and a lamp strip over each bore.

7. Province borders

Build each province's graph from the province plus a 2 km margin, run the strongly connected part on that, then keep edges whose midpoint is inside the province. Border bridges and roads then survive in exactly one province and reach the neighbour's roads at the border.

Steps 1, 2, 3 and 5 make every structure drivable; 6 makes them make sense; 7 makes them look right. Rebuilding streets and walks is about 5 + 5 minutes per province on the GPU machine; carving water changes the ground, so it needs the slower ground rebuild of each province.

12Open questions

  • Rivers: carve the relief (changes the ground of every province) or only draw a sunk water strip with banks along the river (cheaper, no gorges)?
  • How faithful should named structures be: generic arch, truss and swing templates, or one-off models of Bacunayagua, Puente de Hierro and the Bay tunnel portals?
  • Should approaches follow OSM exactly (ways at layer 0 that are really ramps), or be free to start where the profile needs them, as now?
